method: Line-by-line analysis of the complete script: every location, environment, character appearance, action, physical event, prop interaction, emotional reaction, time/place change, narrative reveal, and necessary visual detail was checked against the shot list. Counts are derived from the story, not fixed in advance.

counts_vs_r2_draft.verdict: Counts UNCHANGED from the R2 draft. The line-by-line analysis confirms the R2 breakdown already covers every story beat: no shot was added and none was removed. The estimate that changes is the COST, not the count — audio on without elements ($0.168/s, $8.06) is replaced by audio off WITH elements ($0.224/s, $10.75) in cost-plan.json. (The earlier preflight figure of audio off without elements, $0.112/s, $5.38, was corrected for the elements tier: every shot uses the Nadia character element, so the with-elements rate applies.) The old 8-clip / 48-second / $8.06 figures are superseded as a cost estimate, not as counts.

line_coverage.narration_text: Before the sun wakes the river, Nadia lights the first lantern of the day.
line_coverage.narrative_purpose: Establishing action: the light is kindled. Also the film's establishing shot — the rooftop terrace, the river and rooftops below, and the dawn light are all established inside this shot.

line_coverage.narration_text: She walks the old stone steps down to the water, carrying the light.
line_coverage.narrative_purpose: Journey: the light is carried to the water. Movement through the river-steps location — the full-body walk down the steps, ending at the water.

line_coverage.narration_text: At the river's edge, she sets the lantern on the water and lets it go.
line_coverage.narrative_purpose: Giving action — hands, water, release. Detail shot: a single wide shot cannot show both her hands on the lantern and her face, so the hands get their own close-up.

line_coverage.narration_text: The lantern drifts away, and the whole morning holds its breath.
line_coverage.narrative_purpose: Reaction: hope on her face as the lantern leaves. A different shot from s3a, not a longer single shot, because the camera cannot be on her hands and her face at once.

line_coverage.narration_text: In the market, she gathers marigolds bright as the evening sun.
line_coverage.narrative_purpose: Gathering: flowers for the evening. The market street is established inside this shot — stall, hanging fabrics, shoppers — so no standalone market wide is needed.

line_coverage.narration_text: Rain comes without asking, and she opens her umbrella over the day.
line_coverage.narrative_purpose: Weather endured: the same market street in its rain state. The day is endured, not stopped — the calm reaction in the rain is the beat.

line_coverage.narration_text: At dusk, she lifts the sky lantern high, its flame reaching for the dark.
line_coverage.narrative_purpose: The lift — the climax begins in her arms. A separate shot from the release because the lift and the rise are two different movements.

line_coverage.narration_text: She lets it go, and the river light rises to meet the first stars.
line_coverage.narrative_purpose: The release — the lantern leaves her hands and rises into the sky. The film's closing shot: she watches it go, smiling.

story_beats_checked.beat: Light carried to the river (stone steps)
Time passage dawn -> morning -> golden hour -> morning -> rain -> dusk
story_beats_checked.note: Each time/place change is carried by the cut between shots plus the lighting and environment change inside the next shot; no separate transition shot is needed.

story_beats_checked.beat: One day, one lantern's journey mirrored by the sky lantern

corrections_found_in_analysis.finding: Continuity gap in the R2 shot record: script line l2 says Nadia walks down the steps "carrying the light", but the R2 s2 record showed her walking empty-handed (one hand lifting her shirt hem) and carried no lantern prop. The lit round table lantern from s1 is the light she carries.
corrections_found_in_analysis.action: Shot record corrected to the script (action, motion-prompt subject / hand-prop / body, prop_ids now include prop-lantern-table). The story and narration are unchanged; no new shot was created.

considered_and_rejected.candidate: Standalone rooftop wide establishing shot before s1
considered_and_rejected.reason_rejected: s1 already establishes the terrace with the river and rooftops below inside the shot, and it is the film's first image. A silent wide would have no narration line, breaking the 1:1 line-per-shot coverage, and would add a paid clip with no story beat.

considered_and_rejected.candidate: Standalone market wide establishing shot before s4
considered_and_rejected.reason_rejected: s4's medium shot carries the stall, hanging fabrics and shoppers, establishing the market inside the shot. No narration line exists for a standalone wide.

considered_and_rejected.candidate: River-arrival shot between s2 and s3a
considered_and_rejected.reason_rejected: s2's full-body walk ends at the water; the cut to s3a kneeling at the edge IS the arrival. A separate arrival shot would repeat the same beat.

considered_and_rejected.candidate: Rain-transition shot between s4 and s5
considered_and_rejected.reason_rejected: Same street, weather change only: the cut plus wet cobblestones and falling rain inside s5 carries the change. No story beat is missing.

considered_and_rejected.candidate: Closing wide / end card after s6b
considered_and_rejected.reason_rejected: s6b is the closing shot (lantern rising, she watches smiling). An end card would be on-screen text, which the no-text policy forbids.

proposed_shots_note: No genuinely missing story beat was found, so no PROPOSED shot is recorded. The five candidates above were considered and rejected with reasons; inventing a shot for any of them would inflate the count without a story need.
physical_events: weight shifting in a walking stride (s2)
water rippling as the lantern is set afloat (s3a)
the lantern drifting on the current (s3b)
the basket rising in both hands (s4)
rain falling and splashing; the umbrella unfolding (s5)
the sky lantern lifting away and rising (s6a, s6b)
